scenes.line1: How do you fix any network issue?
scenes.say: Ever get stuck chasing a weird network problem? There's a method that works every time, no matter what tool or platform you're on.

rows.b: Check each step: interface, gateway, DNS, port, listener, firewall, packets
Test halfway, compare working vs broken

scenes.say: Here's the checklist: define the issue, scope it, reproduce it, walk the layers, split the path in half, compare working to broken, change one thing, and document what you find.

scenes.label: Layers
scenes.sub: Interface, gateway, DNS, port, listener, firewall, packets
scenes.say: Every problem sits somewhere on the ladder: interface, gateway, DNS, port, listener, firewall, or packets. Always check each layer in order.
Split the path in half. Test from a working site and a broken one. Compare the results to find where things diverge.

scenes.title: Linux & Windows
scenes.say: Use the right tools for your platform. Netcat, Test-NetConnection, traceroute, and ping help you check connectivity, ports, and MTU.

scenes.question: What's the first step after an error?
scenes.wrong: Run traceroute or ping right away
scenes.right: Read the error message to find the layer
scenes.say: Don't jump straight to tools. Always read the error message first—it tells you which layer to start with.
